title: Reciprocal connections dynamically build consensus between neocortical areas
title_zh: 相互连接动态构建新皮层区域间的共识
abstract: Abstract The neocortex is organized into specialized areas. Although computations within individual areas have been well studied, it is unclear how these regions function collectively and reconcile potential conflicts to form coherent percepts and decisions. We investigated the joint dynamics of primary (V1) and higher-order lateromedial (LM) visual areas in mice using simultaneous multi-area electrophysiological recordings along with focal optogenetic perturbations to causally manipulate neural activity. We used data-driven nonlinear system identification to construct biologically constrained latent circuit models of both areas. This approach revealed that reciprocal excitatory connections between V1 and LM implement an approximate line attractor in their joint dynamics: this selectively slows the decay of congruent activity patterns while accelerating the decay of inconsistent ones, thereby dynamically achieving inter-area consensus. This mechanism predicts different timescales for consistent versus inconsistent activity patterns across areas, which we verified in our data. These findings, together with our mechanistic theory, identify dynamic consensus building as a general principle of distributed cortical computation.
abstract_zh: 摘要 新皮层被组织成专门化区域。虽然单个区域内的计算已被充分研究，但这些区域如何协同工作并调和潜在冲突以形成连贯的感知和决策仍不清楚。我们利用同时多区域电生理记录和局部光遗传扰动，研究小鼠初级视觉区（V1）与高阶侧中部视觉区（LM）的联合动力学，并通过因果操纵神经活动。采用数据驱动的非线性系统识别方法构建了受生物学约束的潜在电路模型。该方法揭示，V1 与 LM 之间的相互兴奋性连接在其联合动力学中实现了近似线吸引子：该机制选择性地减慢一致活动模式的衰减速度，同时加速不一致模式的衰减，从而动态实现区域间共识。该机制预测不同时间尺度的持续一致与不一致活动模式，并在我们的数据中得到验证。这些发现与我们的机制理论共同表明，动态共识构建是分布式皮层计算的普遍原则。
